working_title: Why Is the Periodic Table in This Order?
always_fails: unfinished Explorer hair or melted face
notes: DRAFT only. Do not Flow / mint until Ben PASS on VO v01. If VO is redone, re-time vo_land and rebuild this board. Plate UAT on continuous playback only.
title: Cold open — knife, coin, atom

open_stamp.treatment: No place stamp on cold open; story picture first

set_language: Cold-open journey sets (not one room): wooden bench + gold coin; cartoon gold atom; periodic table (002 look); Greek scroll; glowing glass tube; gold foil; 1913 target lab. Say 'same <beat> set' for continuity within a beat; never 'same DNA'.
continuity_lock: Picture change every ~4–6 s. No Explorer. 0:18 Te/I tap is a hand only (no face).
explorer_lock: NONE this part — never in the first minute. Hand-only at Te/I tap.
forbidden: HARD REJECT: Orbit robot; photoreal; Ken Burns or still push; gore; lava drip / molten bead; underside lamp bulb or shade cup; unfinished flat cards; unfinished Explorer hair; DNA helix; readable text or logos baked into the plate (labels added in edit); twin Explorer; never say 'same DNA' or 'lab DNA' in a Veo prompt. No Explorer anywhere in Part 01. No slow 1:08–1:15 hold — three short beats instead.
motion_lock: Real Veo camera + object motion every plate when mint opens. No freeze-pad.
quality_note: Veo 3.1 Quality for atom glow, tube glow, target glow; Fast only for low-risk garnish.

plates.vo_land: Cut a gold coin in half. Then cut it again. And again.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Wooden bench, a gold coin; a knife halves it, then halves a half — continuous cutting motion at frame 0. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No readable text. HARD REJECT: photoreal, Ken Burns only, Explorer face.

plates.vo_land: How small can you go before it stops being gold?
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Push into the last gold speck; it resolves into a glowing cartoon gold atom — nucleus and electron cloud (ANSWER IMAGE). Continuous resolve. Silent. No Explorer. HARD REJECT: photoreal atom photo, Orbit, Ken Burns only.
Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Same gold atom set. Atom turns slowly; soft glow pulses at its tiny centre. Continuous turn. Silent. No readable text in plate. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, DNA helix.

plates.vo_land: By the end of this film you'll know why the periodic table is in the order it is, and how we proved it.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Periodic table (002 look) slams into frame; boxes light in order along the table. Continuous slam + light chase. Silent. No Explorer. HARD REJECT: garbled letters as hero, Orbit, Ken Burns only.

plates.vo_land: Because in 1869 the table had a secret problem. It was sorted by weight, and some elements refused to fit.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Same table set. A human hand only (no face, no Explorer body) taps Te and I boxes; they wobble out of line. Continuous tap + wobble. Silent. HARD REJECT: Explorer face/body, twins, Orbit, finished teacher OC.

plates.vo_land: If weight was the rule, the rule was broken, and nobody knew why.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Balance scale tips the wrong way under a Te card; an I card slides past. Continuous tip. Silent. Readable card symbols OK if clear; no wall of text. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, lava.

plates.vo_land: For two thousand years the atom was just an idea: the smallest piece, the one you can't cut.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Ancient Greek scroll mood; a stone is chipped smaller and smaller. Continuous chip. Silent. No Explorer. HARD REJECT: photoreal ruins, Orbit, DNA helix.
Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Chip shrinks to a grey bead; chisel slips off; magnifying glass shows nothing but blur. Continuous slip + blur. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, Ken Burns only.

plates.vo_land: Then, in a glowing glass tube, someone found a piece smaller than the atom.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Glowing glass tube; a tiny bright particle flies out. Continuous flight. Quality clean glow (no lava). Silent. HARD REJECT: underside lamp bulb, lava drip, Orbit, Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Then a tiny bullet bounced back off a sheet of gold, as if it had hit a wall.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Gold foil; almost every particle passes through; one bounces back at a steep angle. Continuous stream + one bounce. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, photoreal.

plates.vo_land: And the final proof came from a young physicist with a beam of X-rays,
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. 1913 lab; a row of metal targets glows one after another under a beam. Continuous glow chase. Quality clean light. Silent. HARD REJECT: lava, Orbit, Explorer.

plates.vo_land: who counted what was inside every element.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Same 1913 target set. Each glowing target flips a numbered card 1, 2, 3…. Continuous flip. Cards must be readable. Silent. HARD REJECT: garbled cards, Orbit, Explorer.
Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Back to wobbling Te and I boxes; camera pulls back to the whole table. Continuous pullback. Silent. HARD REJECT: Explorer, Orbit, slow freeze-hold.

plates.vo_land: and a question that started with a knife and a coin.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Knife and coin halves return beside the giant table. Continuous settle. Silent. No Explorer. HARD REJECT: Ken Burns only, Orbit.

plates.vo_land: So why was the table in the wrong order?
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Quick beat: Te and I still wrong, table half-lit — short cut, NOT a slow hold. Continuous micro-move. Silent. HARD REJECT: long still push 1:08–1:15 style, Orbit, Explorer.
Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Candlelight on an old ledger of element weights; pages turning. Continuous page turn. Bridges to Part 02 chapter card. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, photoreal.
